# FindMyDoctor Project Schedule

This schedule follows the recommended 9-week prototype delivery baseline described in Section 3.2, **Project Schedules**, of the SPMP. Parallel work is planned where dependencies and staffing permit.

**Progress status:** Weeks 1–4 are marked done as requested. This status is a project progress marker and is not an independent verification of each deliverable.

**Invoice note:** Invoices generated by the system are prototype payment receipts, not official receipts. The invoice PDF must carry this label.

**System alignment:** The medicine-billing and invoice work below relates to existing documented capabilities for prescriptions, additional charges, cash/GCash payment, secretary-patient conversations, notifications, and private file storage. The detailed invoice lifecycle (invoice numbering and PDFs, void-and-reissue, invoice chat messages, and short-lived signed downloads) is a proposed extension; it is not described as already implemented. The SPMP PDF was not available in the repository, and the [SPMP URL supplied with this schedule](https://claude.ai/FindMyDoctor_SPMP_v1.0.pdf) did not return readable document content during this check, so these additions cannot be independently confirmed as original SPMP requirements.

| Week | Primary activities | Exit evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weeks 1–3 | Initiation, architecture, authentication, RBAC, OTP flows, doctor approval, admin provisioning, and web dashboards. | Approved baselines, role-protection tests, admin seed, and protected routes. | Done |
| Week 4 | Scheduling module (working hours, availability, break periods), capacity calculation (30-minute default), daily capacity configuration, and reservation system foundation. | Capacity calculation tests, schedule CRUD operations, and basic reservation tests. | Done |
| Week 5 | Unified queue management with sequential numbering, concurrency-safe queue assignment, automatic queue reassignment on cancellation with notifications, capacity enforcement across online and walk-in registrations, walk-in registration with temporary password generation, doctor-specific patient record check before booking, and mobile navigation to appointments view. | Booking/queue integration tests, conflict prevention tests, walk-in account lifecycle tests, concurrency-safe queue assignment tests, queue reassignment notification tests, and doctor-specific patient record validation tests. | Done |
| Week 6 | GCash payment flow (static QR code, receipt upload, verification states), additional charges, payment verification, and secretary-patient chat (conversation authorization and messaging). Payment total equals consultation fee plus additional charges. Walk-in patients may pay after consultation with secretary confirmation. Receipt upload never auto-marks payment as Paid (statuses: Unpaid, Pending Verification, Paid, Rejected). Notifications are triggered for new secretary messages and payment verification using the notification module. | Payment state tests, receipt verification workflow, chat authorization tests, private receipt storage verification, total-amount calculation tests, and a test that patient-to-doctor messaging is blocked. | Not started |
| Week 7 | **Records and prescriptions (first):** consultation/visit records, medical history, prescription management, and PDF generation. A visit links to an appointment; a prescription contains items (medication, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions). Prescription-availability notification; patient access limited to their own prescriptions and PDFs. **Medicine billing and invoices (sequentially after prescriptions):** (1) Add MEDICINE charge lines to the visit bill with name, quantity, and unit price, optionally linked to a prescription item. The secretary sets prices, never the doctor. Prescribed medicines the clinic does not stock are not charged. No inventory tracking is included in the prototype. (2) Support cash or GCash payment; the secretary confirms cash directly, and neither method automatically marks a payment as Paid. (3) Handle the balance when an advance payment was already made. (4) Generate an invoice PDF with an invoice number only when payment status is Paid; store it privately, label it as a prototype payment receipt, and void/reissue paid invoices rather than editing them. (5) Add an invoice chat message type and a **Send to patient** action on the secretary web dashboard, with patient notification and download through an authorized, short-lived signed URL. **Parallel track:** AI chatbot integration (safety and data minimization), AI conversation persistence (endpoints: `/ai/chat` and `/ai/conversations`), and server-side-only AI API key handling, run alongside the above as the SPMP allows. | Prescription PDF tests, medical-record association tests, and an authorization test that patients can only view their own prescriptions and PDFs. Billing: totals still equal consultation fee plus charges including medicines; balance calculation tests; no invoice for Unpaid, Pending Verification, or Rejected; void-and-reissue test; a test that doctors cannot set prices; and an authorization test that only the patient in the conversation can download their invoice. Chat: patient-to-doctor messaging remains blocked. AI: safety tests, data minimization verification, and a check that the AI key is never exposed to clients. | Not started |
| Week 8 | Mobile integration with appointments, queue, history, prescriptions, and notifications; end-to-end role workflows. Waitlist feature (join waitlist and waitlist status notifications), patient cancel and reschedule of eligible appointments in mobile app, patient payments view (GCash QR and receipt upload) with invoice list and download, and patient queue visibility. Notifications: appointment changes (cancel/reschedule), prescription availability, invoice availability, waitlist updates, and notices to affected patients after a confirmed secretary/doctor exception or break-period change. Notification module foundation exists from earlier weeks. | Role-based end-to-end workflow tests, mobile feature integration tests, end-to-end test for schedule-change flow (exception/break change affecting active appointments -> confirmation -> affected-patient notification, with no auto-cancellation), end-to-end test for waitlist, end-to-end test for cancel/reschedule, end-to-end test for the billing flow (prescribe -> add medicine charges -> pay -> verify -> invoice -> chat -> patient download), and a check that ADMIN cannot perform clinic operations (schedules, capacity, queue, payments, invoices, consultation records). | Not started |
| Week 9 | Regression testing, performance/concurrency checks, privacy/security review, defect resolution, UAT, deployment, release notes, and handover. Asia/Manila timezone consistency check across appointments, queue entries, schedules, messages, notifications, payments, and invoices. Privacy/security review to confirm Supabase service role key and AI keys stay backend-only, receipts and invoices are not publicly accessible, and mobile/web never access PostgreSQL directly. Deployment as mobile and web clients reaching the backend API over HTTPS. | Timezone consistency results, security review findings, release candidate, UAT approval, and approved prototype release. | Not started |

FindMyDoctor SPMP, Section 3.2, **Project Schedules** (schedule begins on printed page 7; Week 9 continues on printed page 8). The supplied [SPMP PDF link](https://claude.ai/FindMyDoctor_SPMP_v1.0.pdf) could not be independently verified during this update.
